You are given a OSP scheduling instance.

Problem description:
- There are multiple jobs and multiple machines.
- Each job consists of tasks; each task requires a specific machine and has a processing duration.
- A machine can process at most one task at a time.
- You must assign a start time to every task so that all machine conflicts are avoided.
- Tasks within the same job can be in any order, but a job cannot run two tasks at the same time.

Objective:
- Minimize the makespan (the completion time of the last finishing task).

You will receive the instance below:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your schedule using exactly the following JSON format (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": [
    {
      "job": <job_id>,
      "tasks": [
        {
          "task": <task_index>,
          "start": <start_time>,
          "machine": <machine_id>,
          "duration": <duration>
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Rules:
- Include every job exactly once in the outer list.
- For each job, include all of its tasks exactly once.
- The `machine` and `duration` must match the instance for that job/task.
- Start times must produce a valid schedule (no machine overlap).

A restaurant manager asks you to plan the kitchen schedule by choosing the sequence and start times for preparing a batch of customer orders, where each order must visit a specific set of cooking stations exactly once in some order you choose, with no station handling more than one dish at the same time and no dish being worked on in two places at once, so that all orders are finished as early as possible.

A wedding planner needs you to schedule the setup tasks for several venues by picking the order and start times for each task, knowing that every venue requires services from a specified group of vendors exactly once each and the order of those services is not fixed; ensure each vendor works on only a single venue at a time and no venue receives two services simultaneously, with the aim of completing all venue setups in the smallest possible total time.

A film post team asks you to arrange the workflow by deciding the order and start times for processing several footage reels through a set of post stations, where each reel must be processed at each designated station exactly once with no prescribed sequence, and each station can handle only a single reel at a time while a reel cannot be in two stations at once, so the entire batch is ready as soon as possible.

A vehicle fleet supervisor wants a plan that assigns the sequence and departure times for servicing a group of trucks at a selection of maintenance bays, where each truck needs attention at each listed bay exactly once in any order you decide, subject to each bay serving only a single truck at a time and no truck being at two bays at the same instant, to minimize the time by which all trucks are back on the road.

A graphic studio director asks you to schedule the workflow by selecting the sequence and start times for a set of design jobs across several specialized workstations, each job requiring processing at each specified station exactly once and with no fixed ordering between those tasks; make sure each workstation handles one job at a time and no job occupies two stations concurrently, aiming to finish the whole batch as quickly as possible.

A hospital operations coordinator requests a schedule that sets the order and start times for several patient tests across a group of diagnostic machines, where each patient must use each assigned machine exactly once with no predetermined ordering, and each machine can serve only one patient at a time while a patient cannot undergo two tests at the same moment, with the goal of minimizing the time when the last patient completes testing.

A craft brewery manager needs you to plan tank usage by ordering and timing transfers for a set of brew batches that must visit a list of process tanks exactly once each in any sequence you choose, ensuring each tank handles a single batch at a time and no batch is being transferred in two tanks simultaneously, so that all batches finish processing as soon as possible.

A dry cleaner owner asks you to arrange the processing order and start times for a set of garments that require treatment on several machines exactly once per machine with no required order, while ensuring each machine handles one garment at a time and no garment is processed in parallel on different machines, aiming to have all garments finished at the earliest possible moment.

An IT operations lead wants a schedule that selects the execution order and start times for multiple software builds that must run a set of tests on different servers exactly once each in any order you determine, with the constraint that each server runs a single test at a time and no build runs tests on multiple servers simultaneously, to minimize the time when the last build completes.

A photo lab manager asks you to plan the processing sequence and start times for batches of prints that each require work on a set of machines exactly once and in no fixed order, making sure each machine processes only a single batch at a time and no batch is on more than one machine at the same moment, so the entire set of prints is ready as soon as possible.

A construction supervisor requests a timetable that picks the order and start times for several subcontractor tasks at a series of workstations, where each building element needs services from a listed set of trades exactly once in an order you may choose, with each workstation occupied by only one subcontractor at a time and no element receiving two trades at once, to minimize the completion time for the whole project.

A printing press coordinator wants you to schedule the run order and start times for a queue of print jobs that each must pass through a set of press stations exactly once with no predetermined sequence, ensuring every station handles one job at a time and no job is processed at two stations simultaneously, aiming to have the entire queue finished as quickly as possible.

A research lab manager asks you to sequence and time a set of experiments that must be run on several lab instruments exactly once per instrument with no fixed step order, while ensuring each instrument is used for only a single experiment at any given time and no experiment runs on multiple instruments at once, so the batch of experiments completes in minimal time.

A wardrobe coordinator needs a plan that sets the order and start times for multiple costume pieces that each require attention from several specialty stations exactly once and in an order you select, with the rule that each station works on a single piece at a time and no piece is at two stations simultaneously, to get all costumes ready as soon as possible.

A music producer asks you to schedule the recording sessions by choosing the order and start times for several song tracks that must use a set of studios or engineers exactly once each without a set sequence, making sure each studio or engineer is booked for only one track at a time and no track occupies two resources simultaneously, with the aim of finishing the whole album in the least possible time.

An apparel factory planner requests a schedule assigning sequence and start times for several garments that need processing on a collection of machines exactly once per machine with no required order, under the constraint that each machine handles a single garment at a time and no garment is processed in two places at once, so the production batch wraps up as early as possible.

An event tech lead needs you to plan the setup by determining the order and start times for a set of stages that each require work from various technicians exactly once each in any sequence you pick, while ensuring each technician works on only one stage at a time and no stage gets simultaneous attention from multiple technicians, to minimize the time when all stages are ready.

As the IT operations lead, schedule and sequence maintenance steps so that each application receives each required update once at each designated server in any order, with each server handling a single update at a time and no application updated in two places simultaneously, and minimize the time until the entire suite is updated.

As the bookstore manager, organize when and in which order to process returns and repairs so that each book receives each required service once at each desk in any sequence, with each desk handling a single book at a time and no book processed at multiple desks concurrently, and try to reduce the moment when all books are handled.

Have the school facilities coordinator schedule and order maintenance jobs so that each classroom gets each required service once at each service point in any order, with each service point occupied by only one job at a time and no classroom receiving two services at once, and aim to finish all maintenance as early as possible.

Ask the landscaping supervisor to choose timing and order of tasks so that each section of the grounds gets every required treatment once at each specified station in any order, with each station treating only one section at a time and no section undergoing two treatments simultaneously, and reduce the time until the entire project is done.

A home cook asks you to decide the order and start times for every component on the kitchen appliances so that all plates are finished as soon as possible, with each plate required to visit its listed appliance exactly once, no appliance handling more than a single operation at a time, and no plate being prepared in two places at once.

A furniture refinishing foreman needs a plan for routing pieces among sanding, staining, and drying stations so that the last piece is ready as soon as possible, with each item visiting each required station exactly once, each station working on only one piece at a time, and no piece being processed in two stations concurrently.

A small electronics repair shop manager needs a schedule that picks the order and start times for devices across diagnostic, repair, and testing benches so all devices are returned as soon as possible, where each device must be worked on at each required bench exactly once, each bench attends to a single device at a time, and no device is at two benches at the same time.

The community laundry coordinator wants you to order and time the loads through washers and dryers so the whole set of laundry finishes in the shortest overall time, with each load going through each required machine exactly once, each machine handling one load at a time, and no load occupying two machines simultaneously.

The bike shop supervisor wants you to schedule repairs through inspection, parts, and tuning areas so that all bicycles are finished in the smallest possible total time, with each bicycle getting each required service exactly once, each area servicing one bicycle at a time, and no bicycle being worked on in two areas at the same time.

The metal shop foreman needs an ordering and timing plan for parts through cutting, welding, and grinding stations so the last part is completed as early as possible, ensuring each part goes to each assigned station exactly once, each station works on a single part at a time, and no part is at two stations at once.

A pottery studio coordinator asks you to decide the sequence and start times for pieces through shaping, glazing, and firing areas so all pieces finish in the minimum possible timeframe, with each piece visiting each needed area exactly once, each area handling one piece at a time, and no piece being in two areas simultaneously.

global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct cooking stations in the kitchen (e.g., grill, oven, fryer) that can process one dish at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List or identifiers of the individual customer orders (order IDs or plate names) to be prepared in this schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the venues (jobs). Each identifier names a venue that requires services from a set of vendors exactly once each.

global_fields.name: machines

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of footage reels in the batch. Each reel is a job that must be processed at its assigned post stations exactly once.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of post-production stations available (e.g., color, sound, VFX). Each station can process at most one reel at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the post station that must perform this task (must match one of the station_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

global_fields.name: nr_jobs

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of maintenance bays available at the depot. Each bay can service at most one truck at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each truck that needs service. Each identifier refers to one truck/job for which a sequence of bay visits and start times must be planned.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each maintenance bay. Each identifier denotes a resource that can process one truck at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the truck that requires the service task. Used to group tasks that belong to the same truck (job). A truck cannot be in two bays simultaneously.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of a required service entry for a truck. This is an identifier for that specific required visit (not the execution order — the order is to be chosen by the scheduler).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the maintenance bay where this service must be performed. Each listed service for a truck names exactly one bay that must perform that service once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to perform the service at the specified bay for that truck, expressed in the scheduling time units used (e.g., minutes or hours). This is the processing time that blocks the bay and the truck while the service runs.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of specialized workstations available in the studio; each station can process at most one piece at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each design piece to be scheduled (e.g., piece_1, piece_2); these correspond to the job entities that need visits to stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each workstation (e.g., station_A, station_B); these are the resources that tasks require and cannot be double-booked.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or local identifier for this required visit of the piece (used to distinguish tasks within the same piece); this is not a prescribed order — the sequencing among these steps is to be decided by the schedule.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the workstation (from station_ids) where this step must be performed; the piece must visit this station exactly once for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required at the specified workstation for this task, expressed in the instance time units; the schedule must allocate this continuous time interval on the required station for the piece.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patients who need testing; equals the number of jobs to schedule. Each patient will require a sequence of tests (one per assigned machine).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of diagnostic machines available in the hospital. Each machine can handle at most one patient's test at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the patients (job identifiers). Each identifier refers to one patient whose tests must be scheduled across the machines.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the diagnostic machines. Tasks reference these identifiers to indicate which machine a given test must use.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the patient to which this task (test) belongs; must match one entry from patient_ids. A patient cannot undergo two tests at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the diagnostic machine required for this specific test; must match one entry from machine_ids. The test must be processed exactly once on this machine, and machines cannot process more than one test simultaneously.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this test on its required machine (time units, e.g., minutes). This is the time the machine will be occupied and the patient engaged for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the test servers; each identifier is used by tasks to indicate on which server a test must run.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the software build for this task; matches one entry from the 'build_ids' list and groups tests belonging to the same build.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

job_task_item_fields.name: duration

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific lab instrument required for this visit (must match one entry from instruments_list); the experiment must use this instrument once for the stated duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
