global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the technicians. These identifiers are used to indicate which technician must perform a visit/task at a stage.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the stage (job) that the task belongs to. Matches one entry from the global stage_ids list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index identifying one required technician visit for the stage. This is an index for a required task at the stage (not a prescribed sequence); the solver may choose the execution order of these visits.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the technician who must perform this visit/task at the stage. Matches one entry from the global technician_ids list; each listed technician visits the stage exactly once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time for the technician's work at the stage (duration of the visit). During this time the technician is occupied and the stage cannot be worked on by another technician simultaneously.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patients to be scheduled in the clinic. This is the count of distinct patient jobs the schedule must accommodate.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of chairs and devices (e.g., treatment chairs, X‑ray, sterilizer) available in the clinic. Each device can serve at most one patient at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of patient identifiers (e.g., "Patient1", "P2") representing each patient job. Each identifier links to that patient's required procedures.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of device or chair identifiers (e.g., "ChairA", "XRay1") available for procedures. Task machine_id values refer to entries from this list.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the patient who requires this procedure; matches one entry from the 'patients' list and groups tasks that belong to the same patient.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Local index for a procedure within a patient's list of required procedures. This distinguishes multiple tasks for the same patient but does NOT prescribe their execution order (the scheduler decides sequencing).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the chair or device required for this procedure; must match one entry from the 'devices' list. Each procedure uses its specified device exactly once and devices cannot handle parallel procedures.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this procedure on the specified device, expressed in consistent time units (e.g., minutes). Used to compute start and finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of shipments to be loaded at the hub. This is the count of distinct jobs (each job = one shipment) that must visit their required docks exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of docks available at the hub. Each dock can handle at most one shipment at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of shipment identifiers. Each identifier names a shipment that requires a set of dock visits (its tasks). Use these IDs to group all tasks belonging to the same shipment.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of dock identifiers. Each identifier corresponds to a physical dock where a shipment must be processed for the specified duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the shipment this task belongs to. Connects a dock visit record to the shipment that must be loaded there.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique index for this visit within its shipment’s task list. This distinguishes multiple required dock visits of the same shipment (note: this index is an identifier for the task record, not the execution order).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dock required for this task. The shipment must visit this dock once for the given duration; docks cannot process more than one shipment at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required at the specified dock for this shipment (in the instance’s time units). This is the time the dock will be occupied by that shipment when scheduled.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments (alteration jobs) dropped off at the tailor; equals the number of distinct jobs that must be scheduled through the shop.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct workstations (stations) in the shop — e.g., sewing, hemming, pressing — that garments may need to visit.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each garment/job (e.g., G1, G2). Use these IDs to refer to garments when sequencing operations and assigning start times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the shop's stations (workshops/machines), used by operations to specify where each alteration step must be performed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the garment this operation belongs to; must match one of the entries in garment_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index or local identifier for this operation within the garment's list of required steps (used to enumerate tasks; note: there is no predefined processing order among a garment's operations).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the specific station where this operation must be carried out; must match one of the station_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required to perform this operation on the garment at the specified station, expressed in consistent time units (e.g., minutes).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patients to be scheduled for imaging procedures (the number of jobs in the scheduling problem).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct imaging devices/resources available (the number of machines that can perform tests).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List or collection of patient identifiers (each entry corresponds to one patient who requires several imaging tests).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List or collection of imaging device identifiers (each entry names a device that can perform specific tests).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the patient who needs the specific procedure (links the task to that patient).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or identifier for this particular test/procedure within the patient's required set (distinguishes multiple tasks for the same patient).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the imaging device required to perform this test for the patient (the machine/resource needed for this task).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time the patient will occupy the specified device to complete this test (processing time for the task, expressed in consistent time units such as minutes).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of film rolls in the batch to schedule. The solver will treat this as the number of distinct jobs (each roll must visit all required stations).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of darkroom stations (e.g., developer, fixer, wash, dryer) available. Each station can process at most one roll at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the film rolls (job identifiers). Each identifier links to the set of tasks that constitute that roll's required treatments.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the darkroom stations (machine identifiers). These are the resources that tasks require and that cannot be used by two rolls simultaneously.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the film roll this task belongs to (must match one entry in roll_ids). Used to ensure each roll's tasks are scheduled without overlap and to collect completion time per roll.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index number for this treatment step within the roll's list of required tasks. This enumerates tasks for a roll but does not imply an execution order — the solver chooses the order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the darkroom station required for this task (must match one entry in station_ids). Indicates which resource the task needs and enforces the one-roll-at-a-time constraint for that station.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the roll to be processed at the specified station (in the same time units used by the schedule). The solver must reserve the station for this duration when scheduling the task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cabinet pieces in the batch that must each visit their required finishing stations once. This is the count of separate jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct finishing stations (machines) available in the shop that can perform operations on cabinets; each station can process only one cabinet at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (labels) for each cabinet in the batch. These are used to reference each job when assigning sequences and start times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (labels) for each finishing station in the shop. These are used to reference where each cabinet task must be processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the cabinet that requires the task — refers to one entry from cabinet_ids. Used to group tasks that belong to the same physical piece.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index number for a single required operation on a cabinet (unique within that cabinet). It distinguishes the cabinet's individual tasks but does not imply any fixed ordering between them.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the finishing station required for this operation — refers to one entry from station_ids where the cabinet must be processed for the given task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for the cabinet at the specified station for this task (in the chosen time units). This is the time the station will be occupied when that cabinet is processed.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of circuit boards in the batch that must each undergo a set of tests.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available testing devices (testers) that can process boards, each handling at most one board at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the circuit boards in the batch; each identifier links tasks to a specific board.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the testing devices; each identifier names a tester that one or more tests may require.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the circuit board that needs this specific test task (ties the task to a particular board).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or label for this particular required test on the board (distinct within the board). This labels one of the tests the board must visit; its execution order relative to the board's other tests is not predefined and will be decided by the schedule.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the tester device required to perform this test task; the schedule must ensure the tester handles only one board at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time the board occupies the specified tester to complete this test (the time length the tester is busy for this task).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of clients who booked services that day. Each client must visit each of their required stations exactly once; this value tells the scheduler how many separate customers to plan for.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of service stations (e.g., hair, nails, massage) available in the salon. Each station can serve at most one client at a time and is a resource the scheduler must allocate.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the clients (e.g., client IDs or names). Each identifier represents a customer who requires a set of services to be scheduled across stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the salon stations (e.g., station IDs or service types). Each identifier names a physical or functional station that performs specific services and cannot process more than one client simultaneously.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The client identifier to whom this service task belongs. Used to ensure the task is scheduled as part of that client's sequence of appointments and that the client is not booked at two stations at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index or label for a particular service required by the client (distinct within that client). It identifies one of the client's required visits (tasks) that must be scheduled once at its assigned station.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the station that must perform this service (which station the client must visit for this task). The scheduler must ensure the station is free when this task is scheduled.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the service task takes at the station (e.g., in minutes). The scheduler uses this to allocate contiguous time on the station and to ensure the client and station are not double-booked; start times plus durations determine the makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of books in the batch to be scheduled. This is the count of distinct jobs (books) that must each visit a set of stations.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct binding stations (machines) available in the small bindery. Each station can process at most one book at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of book identifiers (job IDs). Each identifier denotes one book that requires a sequence of operations (tasks) at various stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of station identifiers (machine IDs). These are the binding workstations (e.g., trimming, gluing, sewing) that tasks may require.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the book that this task belongs to. Must match one entry from the 'books' list so the task is assigned to the correct book.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: A local index or label for this operation within the book (used to distinguish multiple required operations for the same book). The index does not imply order — the processing order is a decision variable.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific binding station required to perform this operation. Must match one entry from the 'stations' list and indicates which machine resource is needed.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to perform this operation on the specified station, expressed in consistent time units. Used to compute start/finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of phones dropped off for repair — the number of separate repair jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of workbenches in the shop; each bench can service at most one phone at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of phone identifiers (one per repair job). Each identifier denotes a phone that must receive a set of operations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of bench identifiers. Each identifier denotes a specific workbench where certain operations are performed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the phone this task belongs to; matches one entry from the 'phones' list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or local identifier for this required operation within the phone's set of operations. This distinguishes multiple operations for the same phone; their execution order is not predefined and is to be decided by the schedule.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the workbench required for this operation. The operation must be performed exactly once at this bench.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required at the specified bench to complete this operation (use the same time units for all tasks).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parcels in the batch to schedule. Used by the solver as the count of jobs that each must visit their required stations exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of packing stations available. Used by the solver as the count of machines that parcels may need to visit.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each parcel (one per job). Each identifier is referenced by tasks to tie them to a particular parcel.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each packing station (one per machine). Task entries refer to these identifiers to specify which station a parcel must visit.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the parcel that this task belongs to (must match one entry from parcel_ids). Indicates which parcel needs the listed station visit.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index distinguishing multiple required station visits for a single parcel. It is an internal task index (no implied order between visits for the same parcel).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the required packing station for this task (must match one entry from station_ids). Each parcel must visit this station exactly once for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time (in the chosen time units) required for the station to process the parcel for this task. The solver schedules start times respecting station and parcel non-overlap using these durations.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of animals (pets) that must be scheduled for appointments that day. This is the count of jobs the front-desk must plan for.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct treatment rooms or stations available (each corresponds to a machine). The schedule must assign procedures into these rooms without double-booking.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each pet (e.g., names or ID codes). Each identifier represents one job that requires a set of procedures in different rooms.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the treatment rooms/stations. Each machine entry corresponds to a room where specific procedures can be performed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pet that this procedure belongs to. Must match one of the entries in 'pet_ids'.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index that uniquely identifies one required procedure for the pet. This is just an identifier for the task (not a prescribed order — the order pets visit rooms is a decision variable).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the required treatment room where this specific procedure must be performed. Must match one of the entries in 'room_ids'.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Length of time required to perform this procedure for the pet in the specified room (in minutes or other time units). Used to determine start times and to ensure no room or pet is assigned overlapping procedures.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of servers that need maintenance; each server is a job that must visit several rigs for tests.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of test rigs available; each rig can process at most one server at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the servers to be maintained. These identifiers are referenced by each test/task entry as the server being processed.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the test rigs. Each rig_id is used by task entries to indicate which rig performs that test.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the server that needs this specific test. Matches one entry from server_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of this test within the server's set of required tests (an internal label for that server's task; tasks have no fixed order).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the test rig required for this test/task on the server; each server must receive this test exactly once on this rig.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this server's test on the specified rig (time the rig will be occupied when this test runs).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garden beds to schedule; each bed is a 'job' that must receive a set of visits (one per required station). Used by the planner to allocate tasks and compute the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct service stations (e.g., compost pile, watering, weeding station). Each station is a machine that can handle at most one bed at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the garden beds (job IDs). Each identifier identifies a bed that must visit the listed stations exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service stations (machine IDs). Each identifier refers to a location where a bed receives one required treatment.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the garden bed this task (visit) belongs to; links a task entry to a specific bed that must be scheduled for service.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or local identifier for a specific required visit within a bed's list of visits. Serves as an internal label for that bed's task (the order is not preset).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station that this visit requires. Specifies which single-location service the bed must receive for this task (each station can handle one bed at a time).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time (processing duration) that the bed occupies the specified station for this visit. Used to compute when stations become free and to ensure no bed has overlapping visits.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of bicycle frames (items) to schedule through the production line. This is the count of distinct frames that each must visit their required stations exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of production stations available (e.g., welding, painting, assembly). Each station can process at most one frame at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the frames to be produced. Each identifier refers to one distinct frame that requires a sequence of station operations (order to be decided).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the production stations. Each identifier denotes a specific physical station where certain operations on frames must be performed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the frame to which this operation belongs. Used to group operations that must all be completed for the same physical frame.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or label of this particular operation for the frame. This distinguishes multiple required operations for the same frame; the execution order among these indices is not fixed and is a scheduling decision.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this operation. This indicates which production station must perform the operation for the frame (each operation visits its specified station exactly once).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for the operation at the specified station (time units). This is the time the station will be occupied when this frame is processed for that operation.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of manuscripts that must each visit all stations. This is the count of jobs to schedule (each manuscript is a job).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct processing stations (e.g., editing, layout, proofreading). Each station can handle at most one manuscript at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the manuscripts to be scheduled. Each identifier labels a job that must visit every station exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the stations (work centers). Identifiers correspond to concrete stations such as editing, layout, and proofreading.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the manuscript for this task entry; must match one of the manuscript_ids. Links a task record to a specific manuscript.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index identifying this particular task within a manuscript's list of required steps. This is a label (e.g., 1..3) and does not impose an execution order — the actual order is a scheduling decision.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this task (must be one of the station_ids). For example, a value may denote editing, layout, or proofreading — the manuscript must visit this station exactly once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time the manuscript needs at the specified station for this task, expressed in the scenario's time units. Use these durations to compute task start and finish times when ensuring no station handles more than one manuscript at once and no manuscript is processed in two places simultaneously.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of client cases that must each go through a set of panel reviews. This is the count of files that need to be scheduled through the review booths.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of review panels (booths). Each panel can review only one case at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the client cases (files) that must be reviewed. Each identifier uniquely denotes one case to be routed through its assigned panels.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the review panels (booths). Each identifier uniquely denotes one panel that can perform reviews sequentially.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the case (from case_ids) that this review task belongs to. A case appears once per assigned panel.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index identifying this specific review task within the case's list of required reviews. This is an internal task number; the order of these tasks is not fixed and must be decided by the planner.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the panel (from panel_ids) required for this review task. Each such panel must perform the task exactly once for the associated case.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time needed for the panel to complete this review of the case. This is the continuous time the panel will be occupied when performing this task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of loaves in the batch that must each visit every piece of equipment once; governs how many jobs the schedule must include.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct physical pieces of equipment available (e.g., mixer, proofer, oven units); each equipment piece can handle only one loaf at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each loaf (job) in the batch; each id denotes a separate loaf that requires processing on every equipment piece exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each piece of equipment (machines) such as specific mixers, proofers, or ovens; used to assign tasks to physical equipment.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the loaf that needs processing for this task entry; ties the task to a particular loaf in the batch.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of this task within the loaf's set of required tasks (a unique label for that loaf's operation); note that this index does not imply a fixed sequence — the start order is to be decided by the schedule.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific equipment piece required for this task (e.g., a particular mixer, proofer, or oven unit); this task must be processed on that equipment once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this loaf on the specified equipment (time units); the schedule must allocate a continuous time interval of this length on that equipment for the task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of canvases/artworks that must each receive all three services (framing, varnishing, inspection). This is the number of separate jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical service stations available in the workshop (e.g., framing benches, varnish booths, inspection tables). Each station can handle at most one artwork at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each artwork/canvas to be processed. Each identifier represents one job that must visit three services exactly once in some order.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the individual stations (machines) in the workshop. Each identifier corresponds to a specific station capable of performing one of the services (framing, varnishing, or inspection).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the artwork/canvas this task belongs to (must match one entry from artwork_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index distinguishing the required service-occurrences for an artwork (e.g., 1..3). It does not imply order — it simply labels each of the three tasks (framing, varnishing, inspection) for that artwork.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific station where this service/task must be performed (must match one entry from station_ids). Stations correspond to particular resources such as a framing bench, a varnish booth, or an inspection table.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the artwork to be processed at the specified station for this task (in the instance's time units). This is the uninterrupted processing time that the station will be occupied while working on that artwork.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patient samples that must each receive the required set of analyses. This is the number of jobs (samples) the planner must schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of clinical instruments/devices available for testing. Each device can process at most one sample at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (IDs) for each patient sample that needs processing. Each ID corresponds to one job whose tests must all be scheduled.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (IDs) for each clinical device/instrument. Tasks reference these IDs to indicate which device is required.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the patient sample this task belongs to (references an entry from sample_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index identifying a single required analysis (task) within the sample's list of tests. Each sample has one task per required device; this index distinguishes them but does not imply execution order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the clinical device required for this task (references an entry from device_ids). This indicates which instrument the sample must visit for this analysis.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required for the device to complete this specific analysis on the sample, in the scheduling time units (e.g., minutes). This is the processing duration used to compute start/end times.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pieces of equipment that must each visit a set of maintenance shops exactly once. This tells the solver how many distinct items need scheduling.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct maintenance shops available. Each shop can service only one piece at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the pieces of equipment to be maintained. Each identifier indexes a sequence of required shop visits (tasks) for that piece.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the maintenance shops. These identifiers are referenced by each task to indicate which shop must perform that service.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the piece of equipment that requires this specific service task. Used to group tasks that belong to the same piece (a piece cannot be in two shops simultaneously).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index for a particular required service within a piece's list of tasks. This index identifies the task but does not impose an execution order — the solver decides scheduling order per piece.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the maintenance shop required for this task. Each shop_id maps to one of the global shop_ids and indicates which shop must perform the service for the given piece.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required at the specified shop to complete this maintenance task for the piece. The solver must schedule a start time and ensure shop capacity and piece concurrency constraints while minimizing overall completion time.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of film clips that must each be processed through editing, color grading, and sound mixing. This is the count of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of physical work stations available (e.g., edit bays, color suites, sound booths). Each station can handle at most one clip at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each clip (e.g., 'Clip1', 'Clip2'). These are the job names that must each visit every required station exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the stations (e.g., 'Edit', 'Color', 'Sound' or 'Station1', ...). Tasks reference these to indicate which station they must run on.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the clip this task belongs to (must match one of the entries in 'clip_ids').

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: A per-clip task index distinguishing that clip's required services. Each clip has one task for each station; this index identifies a specific task but does not enforce an order — the schedule chooses the processing sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which station is required for this task (must match one of the 'station_ids'), e.g. the editing station, color grading station, or sound mixing station.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The processing time needed for this clip at the specified station (in the instance's time units). The schedule must allocate an uninterrupted interval of this length on the station for the task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of electronic boards (units) in the batch to schedule. This is the number of jobs, each of which must visit every bench exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of benches/stations available (e.g., soldering, inspection, testing). Each bench can process at most one board at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the boards (jobs). Each identifier labels a specific electronic unit that must undergo all required operations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the benches/stations. Each identifier denotes a specific station (soldering, inspection, or testing) that a board must visit exactly once.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the board (job) that this task belongs to. Links the task to the specific electronic unit being processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index identifying one required operation instance for the board (e.g., 1..k). Because there is no predefined order, this index distinguishes tasks for the same board but does not imply precedence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the bench/station required for this task (soldering, inspection, or testing). Specifies which station must perform the operation.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time (in the chosen time units) that the board occupies the specified bench for this task. Used to schedule start and end times while avoiding bench and board overlaps.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cakes that must each visit all required stations. Used by the solver as the number of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct service stations (shaping, decorating, packaging, etc.). Used by the solver as the number of machines available.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each cake (job). Each identifier groups the tasks that belong to that specific cake.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the stations (machines). Identifiers correspond to physical stations such as shaping, decorating, and packaging.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the cake this task belongs to (matches an entry from cake_ids). Groups tasks so the solver enforces that a cake cannot be in two stations simultaneously.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: A label/index for one required visit of the cake to a station. This labels the per-cake task instance but does NOT fix the order — sequencing and start times are decision variables for the solver.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this task (must match one of station_ids). Examples: shaping, decorating, packaging — the station that will process the cake for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required (in the instance's time units, e.g., minutes) for the station to process this cake during this visit. The solver uses this to compute start/end times and to avoid overlaps on the same station or cake.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cars in the queue that must each receive all required services during the shift — this is the number of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of service stations available (e.g., wash, rinse, dry); each station can service at most one car at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each car (job) that must visit the required stations once. Each identifier represents a distinct car to be scheduled.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each service station (machine). Each identifier denotes a physical service area where a car receives a particular step.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the car that this task belongs to; must match one entry from the 'cars' list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of this required service task within the car's list of tasks. This label identifies the task item but does not impose an execution order — the supervisor decides the visit order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station where this task must be performed; must match one entry from the 'stations' list. The car must visit this station exactly once for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time the car occupies the specified station for this task (in the same time units used for the schedule). During this duration the station is busy and the car cannot be in another station.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of chores to schedule. Each chore corresponds to a job that must receive attention once at each of its required areas.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct areas/rooms (machines) in the house where chores are performed. Each area can handle at most one chore at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers or labels for the individual chores (jobs) the household manager must complete. Use these IDs to refer to a chore across its required area-visits.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers or labels for the household areas/rooms (machines), e.g., kitchen, bathroom, living_room. Tasks reference these to indicate where a chore needs attention.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the chore this task belongs to. Must match one of the entries in 'chores' and groups tasks that are different area-visits of the same chore.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or unique identifier for this specific area-visit of a chore (a task within the chore). This is not a prescribed execution order — the manager will choose the sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the area/room where this task must be performed. Must match one of the entries in 'areas'. While executing, the area is occupied and cannot serve another task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time required for the chore to be attended at the specified area (processing time). During this time the chore cannot be in another area and the area cannot handle other chores.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of applications that must be updated. Each application corresponds to a job that requires a set of updates (one per designated server).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct servers available to receive updates. Each server is a resource that can handle at most one update at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of application identifiers (one entry per application/job). Use these IDs to group the update tasks that belong to the same application.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of server identifiers (one entry per server/machine). Use these IDs to refer to which server an update task must run on.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the application associated with this update task — links the task to the application/job it belongs to.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or local identifier of this update task within the application's set of updates. This distinguishes multiple tasks for the same application; no predetermined execution order is implied.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the server where this update must be applied. The task requires exclusive use of this server for its duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to perform this application's update on the specified server (how long the server and application are occupied by the task).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of books (returned or to be repaired) that must each receive their required desk services once; this is the count of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of service desks in the bookstore (e.g., returns desk, repair bench, inspection station); each desk can handle only one book at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the books to be processed. Each identifier refers to one book that must visit all its assigned desks exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the desks (service stations). Each id names a desk where specific tasks are performed; scheduling prevents two books using the same desk at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the book this task belongs to (matches an entry in book_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Local index labeling one required service visit for the book (distinguishes the book's required desk visits); this index is not a sequencing constraint — the order of these services is to be decided by the schedule.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the desk that must perform this service for the book (matches an entry in desk_ids). A book must visit this desk exactly once for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the desk to complete this book's service (in the scheduling time units). This is the uninterrupted processing time the desk is occupied for that task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of classrooms that must be serviced (each classroom is a job that needs a sequence of service visits).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct service points or crews (e.g., painting crew, HVAC station). Each service point can handle at most one classroom at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the classrooms to be serviced (e.g., Room101). Each identifier represents a job that requires a set of services.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service points or crews (e.g., Electrical, Cleaning). Tasks reference these identifiers to indicate where a service must occur.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the classroom that needs this specific service task; must match one entry from classroom_list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or label distinguishing this classroom's individual service task within its checklist (order of these tasks is not fixed and is a scheduling decision).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the service point or crew required for this task; must match one entry from service_point_list and indicates which resource will be occupied while the task runs.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to perform this service at the specified service point for the classroom (expressed in the chosen time unit).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patient spaces (rooms) that must each receive the set of required services. This is the number of jobs the ward manager must schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct service points (e.g., cleaning station, linen service, disinfection station) that perform services on rooms. Each service point can handle only one room at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the patient spaces (rooms). Each identifier refers to a room that must receive every required service exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service points (stations). Each identifier names a place where a specific service is performed and which can process one room at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the room for which this task (service) is required. Links this task to the specific patient space that must be prepared.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Local index or identifier for this particular service requirement for the room. This labels the service occurrence (not its execution order) and is used to distinguish multiple tasks belonging to the same room.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the service point that must perform this task (for example: cleaning, restocking, sanitizing). This indicates where the task must be processed and enforces that that service point can only work on one room at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the designated service_point to complete this task on the given room (in the scheduling time units used). This is the processing time that the schedule must allocate when that service is performed.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct grounds sections that each require a set of services (i.e., the number of jobs/areas to schedule).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of service stations (e.g., mowing, pruning, irrigation) available on the property that can perform treatments (i.e., the number of machines).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for each grounds section that needs treatment. Each identifier corresponds to one job whose tasks are the required station visits.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for each service station on the site. These identifiers are used to specify which station is required for a given service task.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the grounds section (job) that must receive the service for this task; ties the task to a specific section from section_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: A local index for this service task within the section's list of required treatments. The order of these indices is not a processing order — the scheduler may choose any sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the specific service station that must perform this task (one of station_ids). Each task must visit this station exactly once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required for the station to complete this service on the section. Used to compute start/end times under the constraints that a station handles one section at a time and a section cannot have overlapping services.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct plates (jobs) the cook must prepare. The scheduler will plan operations for each of these plates so that all are finished as soon as possible.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct kitchen appliances (machines) available (e.g., oven, grill, blender). Each appliance can handle at most one operation at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each plate to prepare. Each identifier refers to one job whose required appliance operations must all be scheduled (exactly once each).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the kitchen appliances. Each identifier corresponds to a resource that can process tasks (plate operations) sequentially, not concurrently.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the plate that requires this specific operation. Links the operation to the plate whose completion time contributes to the makespan.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index or local identifier of this operation within the plate's list of required steps. This is only an identifier; it does not imply a required order among a plate's operations.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the appliance required to perform this operation for the plate. The scheduler must allocate exclusive use of this appliance for the operation's duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required by the operation on the specified appliance (time units). When scheduled, the appliance is occupied for this duration and the plate cannot be processed elsewhere simultaneously.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of furniture pieces (tables, chairs, etc.) that must be refinished; each of these is a job that must visit every required station exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct workstations available (for example sanding, staining, drying); each station can process at most one piece at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (labels) for each furniture piece to be scheduled, i.e., the list of jobs the foreman must route through the stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (labels) for each workstation (e.g., sanding, staining, drying) used to assign tasks to specific stations.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the furniture piece (from piece_ids) that this task belongs to.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index identifying one required operation for the piece within its task list; because order is not predefined, this index distinguishes tasks but does not fix their execution sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the required workstation for this task (one of station_ids), e.g., the sanding station, the staining station, or the drying station.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required for the piece to be processed at the specified station (in consistent time units), i.e., how long that operation occupies the station.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of devices (gadgets) that need service. This is the count of repair jobs the manager must schedule so each device visits every required bench once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of benches (workstations) in the shop (e.g., diagnostic, repair, testing). Each bench is a resource that can handle at most one device at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of device identifiers (one per job) that require service. Each identifier is used to group the three bench visits for that device and to report completion time for that job.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of bench identifiers (workstations) available in the shop. Each identifier represents a resource (diagnostic/repair/testing benches) used to schedule specific device visits.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the device this task belongs to; must match one entry from 'devices'. It links a single visit (task) to its device/job.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index distinguishing the individual visits for a device (e.g., 1..3). This is an identifier for the task item only and does NOT prescribe the sequence in which the device must visit benches.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the bench required for this visit; must match one entry from 'benches'. Specifies which workstation the device must use for this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the device spends at the specified bench for this visit (in the chosen time unit). Used to compute task start and end times and to determine the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of laundry loads that must be processed (each is a job that needs a sequence of machine cycles).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct machines available (all washers and dryers counted as machines the loads may visit).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for each laundry load (each identifier denotes a job to be scheduled through its required machines).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of machine identifiers (e.g., washer or dryer labels). Each identifier names a machine that can process one load at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the laundry load (links the task to which load it belongs).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of this required cycle within the load's set of required machine visits (tasks are unordered initially; this index uniquely identifies the task entry).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific machine that this cycle must use (the load must visit this machine exactly once for this task).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required on the specified machine for this load's cycle (time units used consistently for scheduling start times and makespan).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of bicycles that must be scheduled through the shop. Each bicycle is a job that requires every listed service exactly once; this tells the solver how many bikes must be arranged to minimize the time when all are finished.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of service areas or bays (for example: inspection, parts fitting, tuning). Each area can handle at most one bicycle at a time and this number defines how many distinct service locations exist.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each bicycle to be scheduled (e.g., 'Bike1', 'B2'). These labels link the bicycle to its required service tasks and are used to ensure each bike receives every required service exactly once.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the service areas/bays (e.g., 'Inspection', 'Parts', 'Tuning'). Tasks reference these identifiers to indicate which bay is required for that service.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The bicycle identifier this task belongs to; must match one of the entries in 'bike_ids'. It ties a specific service task to a particular bike.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: An index or label that identifies a particular service task for the bicycle (unique within that bike's task list). In this open-shop scenario this identifier does not impose an execution order — it only distinguishes the bike's required services so the solver can decide the sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the service area/bay required for this task (must match an entry in 'service_area_ids'), e.g., the inspection bay or tuning bay. This determines which single-capacity resource will be occupied while the task runs.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The processing time required for this task, in consistent time units (for example minutes). This is how long the specified service area will be occupied when performing the task on the bike.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of metal parts in the batch that must each be processed at their assigned stations (cutting, welding, grinding). This is the count of jobs the foreman will schedule to minimize the batch completion time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct work stations (machines) available in the shop (for example: cutting, welding, grinding). Each station can process at most one part at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each part in the batch (labels the jobs). Each identifier is used when assigning that part's sequence of operations and start times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each station/machine in the shop. These names reference where a part's operation must be performed (e.g., cutting_station, welding_station).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the part (references an entry in 'parts'). Used to group the operations that belong to the same physical part.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: A unique index distinguishing one required operation of a part from its other operations. This index is not an execution order — the foreman chooses the actual sequence at scheduling time.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station where this specific operation must be performed (references an entry in 'stations'). Each operation requires exactly this station once.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required to perform this operation on the specified station (in consistent time units). The foreman uses this to set start times so stations and parts do not overlap.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pottery pieces (jobs) to schedule through the studio; the manager must sequence and time all these pieces so they complete as early as possible.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct studio areas (machines) such as shaping, glazing, and firing that each piece may require; each area can handle only one piece at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each pottery piece to be processed; each identifier refers to a job that needs one visit to each required area.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the studio areas (e.g., shaping, glazing, firing); these are the resources that tasks occupy while being processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pottery piece (job) that this task belongs to; used to ensure a piece does not occupy more than one area at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of this task within the piece's list of required processes; the order is not fixed and the scheduler chooses the sequence for each piece.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the studio area required for this task (e.g., shaping, glazing, firing); the task must run on this specific area for its duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time the task occupies the specified area (in the chosen time units); this determines how long the area is busy and affects the overall makespan.
